correctness.rationale: Summing the source equations gives exactly \(z'=-\mu z-\sum_j\delta_jI_j\) for \(z=N-\lambda/\mu\), hence \(S-S^0\le (N(0)-S^0)_+e^{-\mu t}\). This produces an explicit exponential bound for \(I_1\) when \(\mathcal R_0<1\). At equality, the rescaled first-stage variable is monotone and therefore has a limit; any positive limit forces, through \(\delta_1>0\), a persistent negative gap \(N-S^0\), which in turn forces exponential decay of \(I_1\), a contradiction. Stable linear cascade equations then send every later stage and \(R\) to zero and \(N\) to \(S^0\). The positive first-stage eigenvalue proves instability for \(\mathcal R_0>1\). The bundled checker replays the exact algebraic cancellations and representative cascade identities.

originality.rationale: The motivating article proves global disease-free stability only for two and three stages under additional parameter conditions, while explicitly observing a no-extra-condition argument only on the restricted region with total population at most \(S^0\). The present statement removes that region restriction for arbitrary nonnegative initial data and simultaneously extends the disease-free result to every stage count. The closest general matrix theorem requires a nonlinear remainder that, in this model, has the sign \(\beta(S^0-S)I_1\) and therefore does not directly cover initial states with \(S>S^0\). Other inspected all-stage results use permanently removed or SIS architectures and do not imply the stated SIRS result.

value.rationale: The source itself highlights that its DFE conditions are sufficient rather than apparently necessary, supplies simulations outside them, and leaves arbitrary stage count for future analysis. The new comparison resolves the entire disease-free convergence question for the stated architecture with a short structural argument: demographic dissipation makes every initial excess over carrying population transient, after which the first infectious stage controls the feed-forward cascade. This removes a biologically counterintuitive lower bound on immunity loss, removes the lengthy three-stage Condition A from extinction, and scales to arbitrary stage count. It is therefore a meaningful structural closure rather than a parameter substitution or routine recomputation.
